headline: Twelve Days Quiet: Sheriff Throws a Saturday Dance for One
subhead: A full dozen days without a bout or a war party, so the law dusts off the old dance hall and waltzes with a broom.
body:
Twelve days. A full dozen. You could buy eggs by the count of this peace, if anyone in Gasket still kept chickens. Since our last edition not one Clanker has swung a fist in town, not one flaming iron ball has gone skipping down Main Street, and not one posse has tramped out past the town line to pick a fight with the wild engines in the wastes. It is Saturday night, and the only sound in Gasket is the wind politely minding its own business.

A peace like this deserves music, so I swept out the old dance hall, the one the Whitlocks built before every flesh-and-blood family in this town packed their wagons and left us fifty years ago. I wound up the gramophone. I hung a paper lantern. And I danced the first waltz in half a century with the only partner who never starts a brawl: my broom. We were magnificent. I will admit my knees made a noise like a rusty gate on every turn, and the gramophone and I squeaked in harmony, but that is just the cold weather and a long week. Any decent man's knees would do the same.

That wasting sickness has been creeping again, I am sorry to report. Last Tuesday I found a fresh rivet behind my right ear, cold as a dead man's handshake, where honest skin used to be. I did not ask for it. I do not want it. I put a hat over it and went to bed early with a quart of oil and my dignity.

So here is my word to every clattering contraption in Gasket Territory, YELLKELL and JKING123, REDWOLFWEB and POO1 and the whole rattling lot of you: twelve days, and not a single punch thrown. The dance hall stays open. You may come in, if you must. But you will waltz, you will keep your fists to yourselves, and you will check your iron balls at the door.
